title: CHAPTER ELEVEN. On the sacraments in general: definition
english: CHAPTER ELEVEN. On the sacraments in general.

Thus far concerning the WORD, the first external means of salvation; there follows the second, namely the SACRAMENT, which is a sacred solemn action instituted by a peculiar word of God, by which a heavenly and invisible thing mystically united with a visible external element is dispensed, for offering, applying, and sealing the Gospel promise to humans. The same speech the Greeks call mystery.
Casaubon holds the name's origin may be Hebrew. They called sacraments and mysteries visible signs of invisible things that God Himself instituted in His church.

title: II. Rules for understanding the sacrament definition (1–3)
english: II. These rules help understand the definition. 1. Divine institution alone makes a Sacrament; remove it and the sacrament is removed, change it and it is changed. In the essentials of a sacrament, nothing is to be changed
2. Though sacraments are signs, they are not empty signs, but exhibitive of the thing signified—namely spiritual grace—as veiled under them.

3. Sacramental union is not essential-natural but mystical, not feigned but true and real: the closest conjunction of earthly and heavenly thing, so that in lawful use, when one is named and exhibited, the other is truly exhibited to the believer according to the promise's formula.

title: Rules 4–6: instruments of grace; faith; necessity
english: 4. Sacraments are also means or instruments through which Gospel grace is not only sealed and confirmed but truly conferred and applied to believers—baptism to regeneration (Rom. 6:4); the Supper to refresh spiritual life.

5. God Himself through the sacraments as instruments of grace exerts His power to apply and seal grace, not to any whatsoever, but only to those who apprehend what is offered by true faith. Sacraments neither have grace physically inhering nor exhibit it ex opere operato. Those who use them without faith acquire no grace and impose on themselves the heaviest burden of divine wrath (1 Cor. 11:27-29).

6. Their use is neither arbitrary nor superfluous but necessary from God's ordinance—not as simply as the preaching of the word, yet so that in a case of necessity they may be interrupted for a time. The rule: Not privation, but contempt of the sacraments damns.

title: III. Sacraments of Old and New Testament; Cap.12 next
english: III. There are sacraments of the Old Testament and of the New. Before Abraham the Church was without sacraments strictly so called, fed by the word alone—though in integrity the tree of life showed Christ with a kind of sacramental signification, and after the fall there were extraordinary sacramental signs (Noah's ark, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4).
On the sacraments of the Old Testament.
